summary.headline: Aeroflex Q4 FY26 total income rose 38% YoY to INR126.5 crore with EBITDA margin of 23.86%; skid assemblies scaling to 15,000 units per annum.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q4 and FY26 performance, with Q4 total income of INR126.5 crore (+38% YoY), EBITDA of INR30 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR17.6 crore (+57%). FY26 total income was INR443.3 crore (+17%), EBITDA INR99.7 crore (+26%) and PAT INR55.5 crore. The new liquid cooling skid assemblies business contributed about 5% of FY26 sales, with 617 skids sold, and capacity is being lifted from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum within about two quarters. Management flagged design and customer quality-audit bottlenecks that delayed skid supply, and guided FY27 growth of about 35% with base business growth of 15-20%.

financial_highlights.change: Majority of sales in Q3 and Q4

segments.name: Liquid cooling skid assemblies
segments.commentary: 617 skids sold in FY26 for ~INR21.2 crore, all in India and supplied to one exclusive principal; ~5% of FY26 sales, guided to 20-22% of FY27 sales. Average selling price guided at INR3-3.25 lakh per skid.

segments.name: Hoses and assemblies (value-added)
segments.commentary: Value-added products (assemblies, fittings and bellows) were 52% of FY26 sales. Management said hose assemblies remain the core business for the next 2-3 years, with 75-80% of hose assembly sales from exports.

segments.name: Metal bellows
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR8 crore, utilisation below 20%; peak revenue potential about INR80 crore at ~85% utilisation. Targeting 50-60% utilisation in 2-3 years. Management called it the highest-margin product.

segments.name: Hyd-Air (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR31.64 crore; utilisation about 60%. Capacity to be used mainly for in-house fittings and connectors for Aeroflex's own projects.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Domestic share rose to 31% of FY26 sales from 26%, with domestic sales up about 40% in Q4. Exports still about 60%; exports grew in double digits in Q4 per management. Largest international customer is 25-26% of sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total growth guided at about 35%, with base business growth of 15-20%.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin target around 23% (FY26 was 22.6%); around 25% over the next couple of years.
Skid assembly capacity to rise from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum within about two quarters.
Skid utilisation target of 60-70% by March 2027 (March closing month, not full-year average); peak utilisation 75-80%.
At 75% utilisation, 15,000-skid capacity implies revenue of about INR325-330 crore for the skid business.
Some skid supply to international markets targeted within FY27; no finalised plan yet.
Expected sales from new data centre hose products (last-mile cooling, firefighting) from next quarter; annealing furnace due by end of 2026.
capex_capacity: Skid assemblies capacity scaled from 2,000 to 6,000 units per annum; expansion to 15,000 per annum targeted within about two quarters; management said further expansion beyond 15,000 is the ultimate aim but not the current focus.
Two robotic welding lines commissioned to improve automation and precision.
New annealing furnace targeted for commissioning by end of calendar 2026.
Miniature metal bellows capacity at 60,000 pieces; no further expansion planned this year, with capital redeployed to liquid cooling.
Hyd-Air utilisation about 60%, with plans to absorb in-house demand rather than add capex.
demand_pricing: Management said the liquid cooling TAM is about INR3 billion growing to about INR21 billion in 5-6 years (~34-35% CAGR), and liquid cooling is about 10-11% of data centre cost.
Skid supply is currently behind demand, with the principal's design work now done in-house and end-customer quality audits adding time; management expects smoothing over the next couple of months.
Orders for skids are visible only from the one exclusive principal; other customer talks have just begun.
Management said Aeroflex is among the only Indian skid manufacturers and competes more on supply than price; overseas landed-cost pricing for hoses is about 25-30% cheaper than local alternatives.
US tariffs: Section 232 tariff on products reduced from around mid-February; current rate cited as 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Order book for liquid cooling skids and planned utilisation for 15,000 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book not disclosed due to agreement; a full-year pipeline is shared by the principal and broken into quarterly POs. Peak utilisation 75-80%; target 60-70% by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did skid execution lag last quarter's expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Bottlenecks are design finalisation (earlier done by principal, now in-house) and rigorous end-customer quality and welding audits, which management expects to ease over a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the export share decline (from ~69% to ~60%) the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports rose in double digits in Q4; the ratio shifted because domestic sales grew about 40%. Skid sales will be domestic, so the domestic share will rise further.

qa_highlights.question: Metal bellows FY26 revenue, utilisation and path to scale?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue about INR8 crore, utilisation below 20%, ARR about INR12 crore; targeting 50-60% utilisation in 2-3 years, with sales cycles longer than other products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR40 crore income tax demand (AY 2018-19) a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand relates to a reopened assessment on a bank interest waiver from the company's takeover of a stressed entity. Management said disclosures were made and advisers are confident of reversal on appeal; no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and ASP outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Skid margin is in line with company average (not disclosed separately). ASP guided INR3-3.25 lakh per skid versus about INR3.4 lakh cited by an analyst for FY26.

risks_watch: Skid execution depends on design sign-off and end-customer quality audits; delays could push revenue below the 15,000-unit ramp.
Concentration risk: skid business rests on one exclusive principal, and order book is not disclosed.
INR40 crore income tax demand (AY 2018-19) is roughly equal to FY26 PAT and is under appeal with no timeline.
Metal bellows utilisation below 20% with long sales cycles; the 50-60% target is 2-3 years out.
Tariff and geopolitical exposure: about 60% of sales are exports, and management cited West Asia developments and US tariff swings during FY26.
Watch Q1 FY27 for skid revenue ramp, the first international skid supply and the annealing furnace commissioning.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, but guarded on specifics: management declined to share skid order book, skid margins, megawatt equivalents and international customer details, citing agreements and scope. Candid about near-term skid supply bottlenecks and the weak FY26 Q1 and metal bellows ramp.
key_quotes: We have achieved an EBITDA margin of 23.86% in Q4, which also reflects our strong operating leverage and also is a result of the continued improvement in our product mix.
So right now, the tariff on our products has been lowered. We don't have any issues with tariffs as I speak.

But if you see from the hose assemblies perspective, almost 75% to 80% of the business of hose assemblies actually comes from exports, which means that our products, first of all, are meet the quality, which is requirement of the international market.

adds.what: Skid assemblies capacity 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum

growth.why: Management guides FY27 total growth of about 35% (base business 15-20%), backed by skid capacity rising from 6,000 to 15,000 units within about two quarters and a visible order book from one exclusive principal, though other customer orders are only just starting; skid supply is currently held back by design and audit bottlenecks.
